# quantum-learning-copy-cost

> Reproducible Python code for the preprint "The Copy Cost of Incompatibility" (F. Ö. Catak, University of Stavanger, 2026). The paper asks how many copies of a quantum state a learner needs when the observables it must evaluate are incompatible (cannot be measured sharply together). It defines an incompatibility number kappa = 1/eta*^2 from the joint-measurability threshold eta*, proves that for anticommuting Pauli blocks of size G the copy cost is a factor G for every single-copy strategy, and shows that for weakly incompatible qubit pairs at angle theta a joint unsharp POVM costs 1 + sin(theta), less than sharp grouping (2).

Key facts:
- Joint POVM of G pairwise-anticommuting observables: E_s = (I + sum_i s_i A_i / sqrt(G)) / 2^G, sharpness eta* = 1/sqrt(G), kappa = G.
- Qubit pair at angle theta: eta*(theta) = 1/(cos(theta/2) + sin(theta/2)), kappa(theta) = 1 + sin(theta).
- Thresholds are verified by semidefinite programming (CVXPY + Clarabel).
- Joint POVMs are implemented as randomized single-qubit basis measurements; readout noise rescales sharpness by 1 - p01 - p10, and full (asymmetric) calibration removes it.
- All results are simulations (NumPy Monte Carlo; Qiskit Aer with the FakeKingston noise model). No quantum hardware data.

## Notebooks
- [01 operators and SDP thresholds](notebooks/01_operators_and_sdp_thresholds.ipynb): exact joint-POVM checks; Table 1 (SDP thresholds, kappa)
- [02 anticommuting selection](notebooks/02_anticommuting_selection.ipynb): selection on hard instances, grouped vs joint POVM vs sequential halving; Figs. 2-3
- [03 qubit pairs](notebooks/03_qubit_pairs.ipynb): copy cost vs angle for qubit pairs; Fig. 4
- [04 noisy simulation](notebooks/04_noisy_simulation.ipynb): randomized-basis circuits, readout calibration, bootstrap; Tables 2-3, Fig. 5

## Source
- [src/copycost](src/copycost): operators.py, sdp.py, selection.py, pairs.py, style.py
- [src/jointpovm](src/jointpovm): Qiskit implementation (schemes, circuits, sampling, executors, analysis, experiment)
- [scripts](scripts): command-line runs; run_hardware.py is a dry run unless --submit --confirm is given
- [tests](tests): pytest suite
